claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance.
Pack-cementation aluminization at roughly 900 °C for several hours can enrich the surface of cast HfNbTaTiZr with aluminum.
Controlled oxidation after aluminization will develop a continuous Al2O3 surface layer.
The resulting Al2O3 scale will be continuous, adherent, and dense.
During high-temperature oxidation, aluminum at the enriched surface reacts to form Al2O3.
The Al2O3 scale impedes oxygen diffusion into the bulk alloy.
Impeded oxygen diffusion minimizes internal oxidation and oxidation-induced microstructural degradation.
Surface aluminization leaves the bulk composition essentially unaltered.
Preserving the bulk composition will preserve the alloy's yield strength and ductility.
After exposure at 1000 °C in air for 100 hours, aluminized samples will have markedly lower oxide mass gain than untreated samples.
After exposure at 1000 °C in air for 100 hours, aluminized samples will have a thinner and more protective oxide scale than untreated samples.
After aluminization and oxidation exposure, yield strength and ductility will remain similar to those of untreated as-cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Prolonged high-temperature air exposure causes significant oxidation-related degradation in untreated HfNbTaTiZr.
Oxidation-related degradation can compromise the mechanical properties of untreated HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed protective effect is bounded to approximately 1000 °C in oxidative conditions for exposures up to 100 hours.
The stability and adherence of the Al2O3 scale under extended thermal cycling or mechanical stress are uncertain.
